parties:

Vs.

full_judgment: So by operation of sub-section (2) of section 5 of Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 the publication of the disputed house in the official Gazette as abandoned property is conclusive evidence of the fact that the said house is abandoned property and has vested in the Government. The presumption flowing from sub-section (2) of section 5 of Ordinance LIV of 1985 that the Gazette notification showing enlistment of a house as an abandoned property is conclusive evidence that the said property is abandoned property and has vested in the Government is of course rebuttable and the persons interested are certainly entitled to rebut the presumption before a proper forum. We have perused the petition filed by the petitioners before the Court of Settlement and also the judgment of the Court of Settlement. The petition is at Annexure E to the writ petition and the judgment is at Annexure F to the writ petition. Since it is undisputed that the title and ownership of the disputed house remained with the original lessee Md. Moinuddin it was certainly necessary for the petitioners to adduce some evidence to show that the disputed house was not abandoned property within the meaning of Article 2 of PO 16 of 1972 in order to rebut the presumption of conclusiveness of the evidence flowing from sub-section (2) of section 5 of Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 to the effect that it was abandoned property. There is no statement in the petition filed by the petitioners in the Court of Settlement that the original lessee Md. Moinuddin with whom the ownership of the disputed house admittedly remained on the date of coming into force of PO 16 of 1972 did not answer to any of the ingredients which would render a property abandoned property within the meaning of Article 2 of PO 16 of 1972. The judgment passed by the Court of Settlement at Annexure F to the writ petition also discloses that the petitioners did not adduce any evidence to show that the original lessee Md. Moinuddin did not fall within the category of the persons whose property were to be abandoned property by operation of Article 2 of PO 16 of 1972. In fact we are satisfied that there was no attempt on the part of the petitioners to rebut the presumption of conclusiveness of evidence emanating from sub-section (2) of section 5 of Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 before the Court of Settlement. Nor any attempt has been made by the petitioner to rebut the said presumption before this Court. So, since the presumption of conclusiveness of evidence flowing from the publication of the disputed house in the 'Ka' list of abandoned property in the official Gazette remains unrebuted we find that that Court of Settlement was justified in holding that the disputed house was rightly enlisted in the 'Ka' list of abandoned property.
